description: Fix product photo lighting without a studio. Upload a phone snapshot and get soft light, gentle shadows, and clean highlights on glass and metal. Start now.
h1: Product Photo Lighting for Glass, Metal, and Glossy Finishes
lead: Product photo lighting usually takes a lighting kit. Upload a plain snapshot and get a square photo with soft, directional light, gentle shadows, and the glow on glass and gold.
secondary_keywords: skincare product photo with soft light
intro: Glass, metal, and glossy packaging are hard to shoot at home, where a window throws glare in one spot and murky shadow in another. In the example, a square perfume bottle with a faceted cap glows with pale gold liquid, its collar catches a highlight, and soft shadows fall across a marble top scattered with white blossoms.

Light like this makes a product look the way it does in person. It's useful for perfume, serums, candles, watches, and anything with a reflective surface, whether as an extra Amazon image or the first photo on your own store.
tip: Photograph your product against a plain wall with no direct sun on it, so harsh glare from the original doesn't carry into the new image.

steps.d: A phone photo on a table works, as long as the whole bottle or jar is in frame and in focus.
Try "soft morning light from the left, long shadows, marble surface" or "bright even studio light, minimal shadow."
Download the first version, then try warmer or cooler light and keep the one closest to your brand's look.

ideas.d: Warm side light through amber glass or a candle jar brings out the color of the liquid or wax.
Even light on frosted glass and gold caps suits serums, oils, and creams.
Controlled highlights on steel cases, rings, or cookware, without the hot spots of a flash photo.

faq.q: Can I get a plain white background instead of a styled scene?
faq.a: Yes. Describe "bright white background, soft even light" for a clean catalog look, or name a surface and time of day for a lifestyle feel.

faq.q: Does it work on clear glass and shiny metal?
faq.a: Those are the surfaces it helps with most. Upload a photo where the outline of the bottle or case is sharp, so edges and reflections stay crisp.

faq.q: Can I use this for skincare and fragrance listings?
faq.a: Yes. Let the photo show the bottle, the texture, and the finish, and leave claims about results, like smoother skin or all-day scent, out of the image and the listing text.

faq.q: What lighting prompt should I start with?
faq.a: Describe one light source and a simple surface, such as “soft window light on a pale table.” A sharp source photo helps glass and metal edges stay readable.

overview.h2: Shape the Reflection Instead of Fighting It
overview.p: Glossy packaging can look premium in one light and unreadable in another. This template lets you explore a controlled direction—soft side light, an even studio wash, or a warmer tabletop mood—while keeping the product at the center of the frame.

A useful brief names the direction, softness, surface, and shadow before it names the mood. That gives you a repeatable starting point for a perfume bottle, serum jar, watch, candle, or cookware item.

input_guide.h2: Remove the Hardest Glare Before You Start

items.d: Photograph the full product against a calm wall or table with no direct sun cutting across the label.
Turn the bottle or jar so its main panel is visible before you ask for a new lighting setup.
Say left, right, overhead, or backlight, then add whether the shadow should be long, soft, or barely visible.
Mention marble, matte paper, stone, wood, or a seamless studio surface so the reflection has somewhere to land.
Use a gentle highlight to reveal glass edges, liquid color, or a faceted cap.
Keep the label and silhouette clear when a retail listing needs a calm, low-drama frame.
Give candles, tea, or amber bottles a cozy context without hiding the product.
Show the shape of a watch, ring, or pan while keeping glare away from the key surface.
Pale gold liquid on marble with a soft highlight from the left and small white flowers outside the label.
Frosted glass and a gold lid on a pale stone counter under broad, even daylight.
Steel case on dark slate with a narrow controlled reflection across the bezel and no flash hotspot.
A polished pan on a neutral kitchen surface with a large soft source that shows its curve.

after_download.h2: Review the Light Like a Product Photographer

items.d: Make sure edges, caps, straps, and handles still match the real product.
Inspect the label and color closely; do not rely on generated lettering for exact copy.
Keep the warmer or cooler version that matches your existing catalog rather than mixing moods without a plan.

good: Perfume, serum, candle, and beverage packaging
Watches, jewelry, cookware, and other metal goods
A product line that needs a consistent commercial mood
Listings where surface and silhouette matter
not_ideal: A source with a large reflection hiding the product
A label whose exact tiny type must be proven in the image
A product whose appeal depends on a moving light demonstration
